raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
Refreshes the MiniCPM-V 4.7 cookbook's DSPARK numbers against the final head of sgl-project/sglang#41993 (`3457dcf33d`), which includes the restored DSpark draft `rope_dim` fix.

## What changed

- All eight DSPARK benchmark cells re-measured on real hardware (GB300 and H200, 1B / 35B-A3B BF16 / FP8 / INT4), single GPU, `bench_serving` sharegpt with `--flush-cache`.
- The matched off → on TPOT table in the guidance is recomputed from the same runs.
- Accept lengths updated: GSM8K ≈4.5 on 1B at the final head (up from ~2.6 pre-fix); sharegpt accept ≈2.5 (1B) and ≈3.2-3.3 (35B-A3B variants).
- The DSPARK recommendations themselves are unchanged: on GB300 enable only for 35B-A3B BF16/FP8 at low concurrency; on H200 for 35B-A3B BF16 at both concurrencies and FP8/INT4 at low concurrency; off for 1B.

## Notable in the new data

- H200: DSPARK now wins c1 across all four variants (e.g. 35B-A3B INT4 TPOT 3.35 → 2.15 ms) and still wins c16 for 35B-A3B BF16.
- GB300: 35B-A3B BF16/FP8 c1 wins hold (2.97 → 2.56, 3.06 → 2.46 ms); c16 remains a loss as before.
- GB300 INT4 decode is ~2× slower than H200 regardless of DSPARK (kernel-level, reproduced on two independent boxes); the existing guidance to use INT4 on GB300 only for memory savings still applies.

Accuracy cells and non-DSPARK rows are unchanged.

Refreshes the MiniCPM-V 4.7 cookbook's DSPARK numbers against the final head of sgl-project/sglang#41993 (`3457dcf33d`), which includes the restored DSpark draft `rope_dim` fix.

## What changed

- All eight DSPARK benchmark cells re-measured on real hardware (GB300 and H200, 1B / 35B-A3B BF16 / FP8 / INT4), single GPU, `bench_serving` sharegpt with `--flush-cache`.
- The matched off → on TPOT table in the guidance is recomputed from the same runs.
- Accept lengths updated: GSM8K ≈4.5 on 1B at the final head (up from ~2.6 pre-fix); sharegpt accept ≈2.5 (1B) and ≈3.2-3.3 (35B-A3B variants).
- The DSPARK recommendations themselves are unchanged: on GB300 enable only for 35B-A3B BF16/FP8 at low concurrency; on H200 for 35B-A3B BF16 at both concurrencies and FP8/INT4 at low concurrency; off for 1B.

## Notable in the new data

- H200: DSPARK now wins c1 across all four variants (e.g. 35B-A3B INT4 TPOT 3.35 → 2.15 ms) and still wins c16 for 35B-A3B BF16.
- GB300: 35B-A3B BF16/FP8 c1 wins hold (2.97 → 2.56, 3.06 → 2.46 ms); c16 remains a loss as before.
- GB300 INT4 decode is ~2× slower than H200 regardless of DSPARK (kernel-level, reproduced on two independent boxes); the existing guidance to use INT4 on GB300 only for memory savings still applies.

Accuracy cells and non-DSPARK rows are unchanged.

@@ -126,58 +126,8 @@ OpenBMB also publishes AWQ, GPTQ, and GGUF exports and a 1B int4 checkpoint. The - Every recipe runs on one GPU. On H100 the 35B-A3B BF16 checkpoint (about 66 GB of weights) does not fit the default static memory fraction of an 80 GB card; use FP8 or INT4 there. - Pick the quantization by platform. On H200, quantization is a speed win: at concurrency 16, INT4 and FP8 reach 15,808 and 15,280 tokens/s per GPU against 12,103 for BF16, and INT4 has the fastest 35B-A3B decode (TPOT 3.47 ms at concurrency 1). On GB300, BF16 and FP8 decode at about the same speed at concurrency 1 (TPOT 4.36 vs 4.44 ms), and FP8 pulls ahead at concurrency 16 (16,059 vs 14,094 tokens/s per GPU). INT4 is slower on GB300 at every concurrency (TPOT 8.56 ms at concurrency 1), so use it there only to save memory. - SGLang detects FP8 and INT4 from the checkpoint's `quantization_config`; no `--quantization` flag is needed. -- The **DSPARK** row adds `--speculative-algorithm DSPARK` and `--speculative-draft-model-path` pointing at the variant's DSpark checkpoint. On GB300, turn it on only for 35B-A3B BF16 and FP8 at low concurrency; on H200, turn it on for 35B-A3B BF16 at both measured concurrencies and for FP8 and INT4 at low concurrency; leave it off for 1B. Matched sharegpt runs back this (TPOT ms, DSPARK off → on): - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -

- -- Benchmark speculative decoding on real text. Random-token prompts collapse draft acceptance, so they say nothing about DSPARK. For a real-workload reference, GSM8K accept length is about 2.6 on 1B, 4.1 on 35B-A3B BF16, 4.0 on FP8, and 3.8 on INT4. +- The **DSPARK** row adds `--speculative-algorithm DSPARK` and `--speculative-draft-model-path` pointing at the variant's DSpark checkpoint. On GB300, turn it on only for 35B-A3B BF16 and FP8 at low concurrency; on H200, turn it on for 35B-A3B BF16 at both measured concurrencies and for FP8 and INT4 at low concurrency; leave it off for 1B. The matched DSPARK on/off cells in the benchmark cards above back this. +- Benchmark speculative decoding on real text. Random-token prompts collapse draft acceptance, so they say nothing about DSPARK. For a real-workload reference, GSM8K accept length is about 4.5 on 1B (measured at the final PR head); in the sharegpt benchmark, accept length is about 2.5 on 1B and 3.2-3.3 on the 35B-A3B variants. - Every command carries `--reasoning-parser auto --tool-call-parser auto`. SGLang resolves both from the chat template, to `qwen3` for reasoning and `qwen3_coder` for tool calls, so the thinking trace lands in `message.reasoning_content` and tool calls in `message.tool_calls` (see §3.1 and §3.2). To turn either off, toggle it in the **Parsers** card of the [Playground](#playground). - Thinking is on by default. To get a direct answer for one request, pass `"chat_template_kwargs": {"enable_thinking": false}` (in the OpenAI Python client, `extra_body={"chat_template_kwargs": {"enable_thinking": False}}`); `reasoning_content` then comes back empty. - Image and video requests need no extra server flags.
